decisions.question: e-21605

source.question: e-21605
source.value:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x)$ to $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the LTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

- After the first step, we have $y_\text{new} = 0.925.$ So, the LTE of the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{1} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.2)-0.925 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.4)-0.925 \\  & ≈-0.004.\end{aligned}
$$

- After the second step, we have $y_\text{new} = 0.692.$ So, the LTE of the second step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{2} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.4)-0.692 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.8)-0.692 \\  & ≈0.005.\end{aligned}
$$

- After the third step, we have $y_\text{new} = 0.368.$ So, the LTE of the third step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{3} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(0.6)-0.368 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.2)-0.368 \\  & ≈-0.006.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $n$ | $x$ | $y$ | $\tau_n$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.000$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.2$ | $0.925$ | $-0.004$ |
| $2$ | $0.4$ | $0.692$ | $0.005$ |
| $3$ | $0.6$ | $0.368$ | $-0.006$ |

$$
y' = -\sin x, \qquad y(0) = 1
$$

source.value:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x)$ to $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution is $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x) = \cos x.$ So, the $y$-value at the start of the step $x=1$ is $y_{\textrm{exact}}(1)=\cos(1).$

Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(1) \\  & =-0.8415.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1)\cdot Δx \\  & =-0.8415\cdot 0.2 \\  & ≈-0.1683.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at $x_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the step starting at $x=1{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{6} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.2)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)+Δy) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.2)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-0.1683) \\  & ≈-0.010\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-21214
source.value:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x)$ to $x_\text{new} = x + \Delta x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is $y_{\textrm{exact}}(x) = x^3.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at a step starting at $x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3})^{′}=3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment given by the numerical method is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at $x_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & =(x+Δx)^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy) \\  & =[{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}]-[{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx] \\  & ={x}^{3}-{x}^{3}+(3{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2})\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3} \\  & =3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-21218
source.value:
The global truncation error (GTE) is the total error accumulated after several steps of a numerical method. The GTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x_{n-1}$ to $x_n = x_{n-1} + \Delta x$ is

$$
e_n = y(x_n) - y_n,
$$

where $y(x_n)$ is the exact value at $x_n,$ and $y_n$ is the numerical value produced after $n$ steps.

We are given the numerical values $y_n$ produced at each step in the table. Now, we compute the exact value $y(x_n)$ at each value of $x_n{:}$

- The exact value at $x_0=0$ is $y(0) = \sqrt{0 + 2} = \sqrt{2}.$

- The exact value at $x_1=0.3$ is $y(0.3) = \sqrt{0.3 + 2}.$

- The exact value at $x_2=0.6$ is $y(0.6) = \sqrt{0.6 + 2}.$

- The exact value at $x_3=0.9$ is $y(0.9) = \sqrt{0.9 + 2}.$

Let's add these values to the table.

| $n$ | $x_n$ | $y_n$ | $y(x_n)$ | $e_n$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.414$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.3$ | $1.480$ | $\sqrt{2.3}$ |  |
| $2$ | $0.6$ | $1.570$ | $\sqrt{2.6}$ |  |
| $3$ | $0.9$ | $1.650$ | $\sqrt{2.9}$ |  |

Finally, we find the GTE at each step, rounding to three decimal places in each case:

- The GTE of the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{1} & =y({x}_{1})-{y}_{1} \\  & =\sqrt{2.3}-1.480 \\  & ≈0.037.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the second step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{2} & =y({x}_{2})-{y}_{2} \\  & =\sqrt{2.6}-1.570 \\  & ≈0.042.\end{aligned}
$$

- The GTE of the third step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}_{3} & =y({x}_{3})-{y}_{3} \\  & =\sqrt{2.9}-1.650 \\  & ≈0.053.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $n$ | $x_n$ | $y_n$ | $y(x_n)$ | $e_n$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $1.414$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.3$ | $1.480$ | $\sqrt{2.3}$ | $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{0.037}$ |
| $2$ | $0.6$ | $1.570$ | $\sqrt{2.6}$ | $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{0.042}$ |
| $3$ | $0.9$ | $1.650$ | $\sqrt{2.9}$ | $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid gainsboro]{0.053}$ |
